title: Geo-consistent quota epoch alignment with predictive grace allocations
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement:
Customers in multi-region setups are seeing inconsistent quota reset times and transient overage rejects when their tenant's reserved capacity leases are shifted between regions or when their org spans zonal time boundaries. Current behavior: quota epochs are anchored to a single UTC-aligned epoch or tenant-configured timezone, and reserved pools trigger independent resets leading to temporary double-debits or lost burst buckets during cross-region failovers. This ticket designs and implements a geo-consistent epoch alignment strategy with a predictive grace allocation layer that:
- Anchors tenant epochs to a canonical tenant epoch while permitting region-local sliding offsets for short-circuit failover.
- Predicts upcoming quota resets and allocates small temporary grace balances to reserved tenants to avoid spurious rejections during cross-region lease handoffs.
- Provides audit trails for any predictive allocations and automatic reconciliation within a bounded timeframe to preserve billing correctness.

Goals and success criteria:
- Eliminates customer-facing rejects during planned cross-region maintenance and automatic failovers for reserved capacity tenants 99.9% of the time in e2e simulations.
- Ensures no permanent net change to customer billable units: predictive allocations are fully reconciled within 24 hours or converted to a formally billable adjustment with customer notification.
- Provides traceable audit logs and a reversible migration path for tenants on older quota anchoring schemes.

Technical design (summary):
1) Canonical epoch controller service: a lightweight service maintains tenant canonical epoch metadata (anchor timezone, anchor offset, epoch length, last-reset timestamp). This service exposes a read-only cache to region-local quota managers.
2) Region-local epoch adapters: each region maintains a local adapter that keeps a small sliding offset (<= 15 minutes configurable) relative to canonical epoch to support low-latency failover without waiting for canonical updates.
3) Predictive grace allocator: a bounded short-lived credit system that temporarily increases the tenant's burst bucket by an elastic grace amount when the adapter detects a pending epoch boundary within a configurable winddown window. Allocations are ephemeral, logged, and reconciled via compensation on the canonical ledger.
4) Reconciliation pipeline: reconcile predictive allocations by comparing region usage against canonical ledger, emitting either a no-op, a zero-sum internal transfer, or a billable adjustment after customer-visible evaluation.
5) Safety controls: rate-limits on predictive allocations, per-tenant caps, and circuit-breakers that disable prediction if reconciliation lag exceeds thresholds.

Data model (flat view for implementation):
- tenant_epoch_meta_id (string key)
- anchor_timezone (string)
- canonical_epoch_start (ISO timestamp)
- region_offset_seconds (string integer)
- predictive_grace_tokens (string integer)
- last_reconciled_at (ISO timestamp)

Migration plan:
- Phase 1 (read-only): deploy canonical epoch controller in read-only mode and populate from current tenant leases. Run for two cycles to collect telemetry.
- Phase 2 (adapter rollout): enable region-local adapters in canary region with predictive grace disabled. Verify epoch alignment metrics.
- Phase 3 (predictive on): enable predictive grace in canary for 5% of reserved tenants with strict caps, monitor reconciliation and billing diffs.
- Phase 4 (ramp): increase percentage and roll to all regions; run forced reconciliation sweep after 24 hours for canary tenants to validate accounting.
- Backout: region adapters can be configured to ignore canonical controller and fall back to current behavior; canonical controller supports forced-anchor reset to revert tenants to previous state.

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
- e2e test harness simulating cross-region failover shows <0.1% unexpected token rejects for reserved tenants at 95th percentile.
- Reconciliation job closes >99% of predictive allocations within 24 hours without producing a net unhandled debit.
- Observability: dashboard exists with metrics: predictive_allocations_total, predictive_allocations_reconciled, reconciliation_lag_seconds, anchor_sync_error_rate.
- Audit logging: every predictive allocation has trace_id and is visible in billing audit exports.

Rollout & monitoring plan:
- Start with canary on us-west-2 with 5% reserved tenants. Monitor for 72 hours for token rejects and billing anomalies.
- Add synthetic load tests that exercise epoch boundary edge cases (DST shifts, leap second simulation, tenant timezone migrations).
- Alert thresholds: reconciliation_lag_seconds > 3600 -> P1; reconciliation_failures_rate > 0.5% in 1h -> P0; predictive_allocations_reconciled_rate < 98% in 24h -> P1.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for canonical epoch controller, adapter logic, and predictive allocator.
- Integration tests between region adapter and reconciliation pipeline using nightly cluster with simulated clock skew.
- Property-based tests to ensure invariants: predictive allocations never exceed configured cap; total net tokens across regions equals canonical ledger after reconciliation.

Operational runbooks (summary):
- If reconciliation lag rises: temporarily disable predictive allocations and run manual reconciliation sweep.
- If customers report unexpected charges: generate per-tenant audit export and run targeted compensation procedure (manual approval required for adjustments > $500).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: predictive allocations could be abused to skirt hard quota limits. Mitigation: per-tenant caps, global rate limiter, and a short TTL for grace tokens.
- Risk: reconciliation divergence due to clock skew. Mitigation: enforce monotonic logical clocks for counters and use canonical controller authoritative timestamps.

- Legal & Compliance: sign-off required for any automatic bill adjustments > $1000 per tenant (not in this scope)
- Owner: Liam O'Connor (ENG)
